facts.condition: For any finite-auxiliary, two-use Marton candidate whose block sum exceeds the established randomized time-sharing benchmark: each input-one marginal lies strictly between 0.375 and 0.625; their sum lies strictly between 0.85 and 1.15; the combined mutual dependence of the two same-receiver output pairs is below 0.04375 bits; and the absolute input covariance is below 0.175. Within the reflected one-parameter input family, the family parameter must additionally lie strictly between 0.125 and 5/13.

assumptions: All information quantities in the condition refer to the full two-symbol block.
Previously accepted ledger results provide the governing Marton upper envelopes and the exact randomized time-sharing comparison level.
The channel acts independently across the two coordinates, and all Marton auxiliary alphabets are finite.
The stated restrictions are only feasibility tests for a strict improvement; they neither construct one nor exclude every possible one.
